summary: Increased inference latency and intermittent request timeouts for streaming endpoints - suspected API gateway / load balancer timeouts and proxy buffering
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Health, dedicated) reports increased latency and intermittent timeouts when using streaming generation endpoints. Customer observes requests that previously streamed tokens across multiple seconds (or minutes) now failing with 504/502/499 and a large spike in p95 latency for streaming endpoints. This appears to have started after an infra change in late Feb.

Impact:
- End users see long waits, partial or no response from /v1/stream endpoints.
- Retries increase and some client-side workflows hit error budgets.
- Affects multiple model sizes (7B and 14B) on the customer's dedicated pool in us-east.

Environment:
- Redwood dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-us-east), prod (us-east-1)
- Ingress: ingress-nginx (customer-dedicated-ingress) fronted by AWS ALB and internal NGINX proxy in front of serving runtime.
- Models: redwood-7b-v2 (streaming), redwood-14b-quant (streaming).

Observed behavior:
- p50 increased by ~120ms, p95 increased from ~800ms to ~6s for streaming responses.
- Error types: 504 Gateway Timeout from ALB, 502 Bad Gateway from internal proxy, 499 Client Closed Request in nginx-access logs.
- Reproducible when generating >2s of tokens or slow token emission patterns.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming responses begin delivering tokens shortly after generation starts and keep a persistent connection for the duration of the stream; timeouts should be aligned with model run time (configurable).

Steps / notes are below and investigation details are in the Investigation field.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From customer's network, send a streaming request to /v1/stream with prompt that produces ~10-20 tokens with model redwood-7b-v2 (use chunked transfer encoding).
2) Observe connection behavior via curl: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -d @request.json
3) Reproduce a long-tail token emission by inserting a slow token callback server-side or by using prompt that yields long token generation (~5-30s).
4) Confirm errors in access logs: 504 from ALB, 502 from internal proxy, or 499 in nginx.
logs: 2026-03-02T11:42:04Z nginx[error]: *23456 upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.12.8.9, server: _, request: "POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.20.3.12:8080/", host: "api.redwood.example"
2026-03-02T11:42:06Z customer-client: HTTP/1.1 499 Client Closed Request trace=tr_1a2b3c
investigation:
Initial hypothesis: connection lifetimes and proxy buffering caused by gateway/load balancer and nginx ingress config are preventing streaming responses from reaching the client and/or causing connections to be closed early. Activities performed:
- Pulled ALB and nginx config (ingress-nginx) for the customer's dedicated pool.
- Reviewed recent infra changes: on 2026-02-28 a platform change reduced ALB idle timeout from 300s to 30s for a set of dedicated pools to limit open connections. Change was rolled as part of autoscaling behavior tweak (PR #1287).
- ingress-nginx had proxy_buffering enabled globally and default proxy_buffer_size set to 8k; proxy_read_timeout was default (60s).
- Observed that streaming endpoints emit initial tokens quickly but then pause (slow token emission pattern) which, combined with a short ALB idle timeout and buffering behavior, causes the ALB to close the connection (504) or internal nginx to treat the stream as stalled and return 502/499.
- No evidence of model runtime failures; serving runtime logs show generation continuing to completion in the backend.

Key findings:
- ALB idle timeout set to 30s is too short for certain streaming sessions where token emission has pauses >30s.
- proxy_buffering causes nginx to buffer upstream responses until buffer fills or upstream completes; for streaming endpoints this prevents incremental flush to client unless proxy_buffering is disabled for those routes.
- The combination of short ALB idle timeout + buffering leads to observed 504/502/499 patterns.

Action items proposed:
- Increase ALB idle timeout for affected dedicated pools to 300s (align with previous defaults) or set per-route keepalive for streaming endpoints.
- Disable proxy_buffering (proxy_buffering off) for /v1/stream and ensure proxy_buffer_size and large_client_header_buffers are increased to accommodate large authorization headers.
- Ensure chunked transfer encoding and Transfer-Encoding: chunked is preserved through ingress.
- Add tests to platform CI to validate streaming passthrough (end-to-end) after ingress and ALB changes.
resolution:
Mitigation and fix applied:
- 2026-03-03 22:10 UTC: Increased ALB idle timeout from 30s to 300s for customer-dedicated-us-east (rollback plan in PR #1292).
- 2026-03-03 22:28 UTC: Deployed ingress-nginx config change for customer pool: proxy_buffering off for /v1/stream, proxy_buffer_size increased to 64k, large_client_header_buffers increased to 4 32k, proxy_read_timeout increased to 300s. Config change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1292.
- Verified by running reproducible script from Steps to Reproduce: streaming sessions now maintain connection and tokens are delivered incrementally. Post-deploy metrics: p95 latency for streaming down from ~6s to ~950ms, 504/502/499 error rate on route reduced by >95% for customer traffic.
- Customer confirmed in support channel (#support-acme) that their integration is back to expected behavior (Jasmine Lee, Acme Health).

Follow-ups:
- Add per-route streaming healthcheck / synthetic to platform monitoring.
- Add an automated test in platform CI that ensures proxy_buffering is disabled for streaming endpoints.
- SRE to review other dedicated pools for accidental ALB idle timeout reduction and remediate as needed.

Ticket resolved and will be closed after 48h of stable metrics.
